(This Evening through Monday)...
Issued at 229 PM EDT Mon Oct 12 2026

Near record breaking warmth is expected through Tuesday as a broad 
upper level ridge expands across the Ohio Valley. A frontal boundary 
will move into the area for midweek with periodic rain and storms 
beginning Tuesday night and persisting through Thursday. Much cooler 
air will expand across the region Friday into the weekend.

Rest of This Afternoon through Thursday 

Warm and breezy afternoon in progress as pockets of mid and high 
clouds drift across the region. 18Z temperatures ranged from the mid 
70s east to the mid and upper 80s in the lower Wabash Valley.

Summer has reappeared across the Ohio Valley as a large ridge aloft 
centers over the region. Southwest winds are advecting progressively 
warmer and more humid air into the forecast area and will keep 
temperatures well above normal over the next 36 hours or so. A few 
locations may reach 90 this afternoon in the lower Wabash Valley 
with 80s anticipated most all other locations. Mid and high clouds 
will continue to move across the region at times through Tuesday 
with breezy W/SW winds resuming Tuesday afternoon.

A frontal boundary across the northern Plains this afternoon will 
slowly drift southeast and be across northern Indiana by Tuesday 
afternoon. Deep moisture is lacking along the front with any 
rainfall well to the north in the Great Lakes in the vicinity of a 
stronger surface low early Tuesday. As the low continues into New 
York state late Tuesday the frontal boundary will become 
quasi-stationary and near parallel to the upper flow regime. 

As the boundary slowly slides south into the forecast area Tuesday 
night and Wednesday...much deeper moisture associated with Hurricane 
Simon currently off the Mexican Pacific coast will advect northeast 
into the region. This will serve as a catalyst to an expansion of 
more widespread convection into the forecast area from the northwest 
late Tuesday night and continuing into Wednesday with PWATS rising 
to near 2 inches courtesy of the rich plume of tropical moisture 
sidling up the frontal boundary. Multiple surface wave riding along 
the front will further aid in widespread rain into Wednesday evening 
before diminishing as the boundary settles near the Ohio River. 

After a short break Wednesday night...additional showers and storms 
will be possible Thursday as the front pulls back north in response 
to a surface low ejecting out of the Rockies and increased upper jet 
phasing. There remains at least some potential for a few stronger 
storms...especially ahead of a strong cold front Thursday afternoon 
and evening but uncertainty in cloud cover and available instability 
makes that solution questionable at this point in time. 1 to 2 
inches of rain is possible focused especially across the northern 
half of the forecast area by Thursday evening 

Temps...the combination of very warm 850 temps...breezy W/SW winds 
and some form of compressional heating in advance of the frontal 
boundary will aid in much of the forecast area warming into the 
upper 80s Tuesday afternoon. A few spots reaching the lower 90s 
remains a distinct possibility over the western portions of the 
forecast area. The KIND record high of 86 degrees from 1975 is in 
danger of being tied or broken. Clouds and periodic rain will keep 
temps in the low and mid 80s Wednesday with a muggy airmass. 
Thursday highs will largely be in the 70s before much cooler air 
arrives for Friday and Saturday. Lows tonight and Tuesday night 
especially will be more typical of mid-late summer peaking in the 
mid and upper 60s.

Thursday Night Through Monday

The aforementioned cold front will sweep across the region Thursday 
night and early Friday with any lingering threats for showers and 
storms ending. In the wake of the frontal passage...the upper trough 
will settle and amplify across much of the eastern half of the 
country into the first part of the weekend before shifting east by 
Sunday. A much cooler airmass will overspread the region as a result 
but a change from model guidance over the last few days is that the 
more progressive flow aloft would support temperatures recovering 
more quickly late weekend into early next week. 

The coolest air will advect into the area Friday and Saturday. 
Intense cold advection combined with a sharp pressure gradient 
behind the front will likely bring some of the strongest gradient 
winds of the Fall so far Friday with gusts peaking at 35 to 40 mph. 
Winds will relax Friday night into Saturday as a 1035mb surface high 
moves across the region. Return flow will develop as early as Sunday 
with the high moving east into the Mid Atlantic region. Deep 
subsidence supports an extended period of mainly clear skies... 
especially over the weekend as cyclonic flow aloft wanes.
